text: After this you can explain what a configuration status record needs to show.

Status accounting is the ongoing record of selected items, their accepted revisions, requested changes, decisions and implementation. A useful record identifies the accepted design. It separately identifies what is present on each unit. The distinction matters when multiple versions operate at once. A blank field is unknown, not proof that nothing happened.

items: Find the item identity and unit identity. You should see: The record points to one version or unit. If not: Resolve duplicate or missing identifiers.
Read the approved description and pending requests. You should see: Design approval is visible separately from work status. If not: Request the missing decision evidence.
Check the actual installed or released revision. You should see: There is dated evidence of that state. If not: Report unknown rather than guessing.
Reconcile differences and publish a corrected view. You should see: Reviewers can rely on the report within its stated limits. If not: Keep conflicting states open for investigation.
Two example units may have the same case marking while running different software. Recording the software version for each unit avoids assuming they are identical.
Inferred: Twelve example items need a modification. Seven are verified, two have unknown status, and three remain pending. Verified, unknown and pending are distinct states.

text: Use separate fields for approved design and verified implementation.
A single free-text "current" field hides important distinctions.

items: Assuming no entry means no modification The record may simply be incomplete. Fix: Mark the value unknown and request evidence.
